specification.outcome: A user can create an ordinary Backlog task or amend an existing Backlog task specification through normal conversation without starting or depending on a campaign and without beginning task work.

scenarios.name: create an ordinary backlog task
given: the signed task board is writable
when: the user asks Pi in normal conversation to create a ticket with a title and description
then: the deterministic host publishes a signed ordinary task creation event
the task remains unclaimed in Backlog without campaign provenance

scenarios.name: create a specified backlog task
given: the signed task board is writable
the user provides a complete canonical specification
then: the deterministic host publishes the task and its exact canonical specification
the task remains Backlog and no readiness review or claim begins

scenarios.name: amend a backlog specification without starting work
given: an existing task is unclaimed in Backlog
when: the user asks Pi to replace its canonical specification
then: the deterministic host publishes the amended specification
the task remains unclaimed in Backlog without readiness review or worktree creation

scenarios.name: reject lifecycle and authority violations
given: the board is read-only or the target task is absent, claimed, Ready, In Progress, or Done
when: ordinary task creation or specification amendment is requested
then: the host returns a stable typed denial
no task, readiness, claim, campaign, or worktree event is published

acceptanceCriteria: The model-facing workflow request schema has closed ordinary task creation and Backlog specification-amendment operations.
Ordinary task creation never requires or creates a campaign checkpoint.
Create and amend operations do not implicitly promote, prioritize, review, claim, or start a task.
Task identifiers, event coordinates, specifications, signatures, and fast-forward publication remain host-derived and validated.
Normal-language guidance directs ticket creation and editing through the deterministic operations rather than campaign goals or slash-command choreography.
exclusions: Automatically starting newly created or amended tasks
Adding title or description amendment after task creation
Weakening signed task publication or lifecycle checks
specification.architectureImplications: Extend the closed workflow request algebra and deterministic host dispatcher with ordinary create-task and specify-task decisions. Keep task event construction, identifiers, signing, publication, and lifecycle authority in the host; model inference supplies semantic intent but grants no authority.
